finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The code opens a specific device file without any user input or dynamic parameters. There is no attacker-controlled data involved in the operation.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The open() call uses a hard‑coded string literal ("/dev/ttyS0"); no user input or untrusted data is concatenated or processed before the call. The source is not untrusted, so there is no injection path.

finding.title: Improperly Controlled Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
finding.assumptions: The code opens a specific device file without any user input or dynamic parameters. There is no attacker-controlled data involved in the operation.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code opens a fixed, compile‑time constant path '/dev/ttyS0' with no use of any user‑controlled data. The source of data is not an untrusted input; it is a literal string in the source code. There is no path from an attacker‑controlled source to the sink, nor any dynamic string construction that could be influenced by an attacker. Therefore, the reported code injection risk does not exist.
